training_data: SLAS-1 (Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study, National University of Singapore; community-dwelling residents of South East Singapore, recruited 2003-2004): 1,601 cognitively normal participants with follow-up (163 incident MCI/dementia); logistic model converted to a 0-11 point risk index, AUC 0.73
test_data: SLAS-2 (same study and institution; residents of South West Singapore, recruited 2009-2013): 3,051 cross-sectional (AUC 0.74) and 1,323 followed CN participants (incident AUC 0.74); plus a field questionnaire version given to 437 people in a community intervention project (194 enrolled), assessed only against RBANS scores
reason: SLAS-2 is a second recruitment wave of the same Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study, run by the same institution in the same country, so under the audit rule it is not an external institution even though the authors call it external validation; a fixed score applied to a separate same-study cohort is V3. The community field project only relates the questionnaire score to RBANS scores in people scoring 6 or more, with no MCI outcome, so it does not validate the classifier.

quotes.quote: DESIGN: Two independent population-based cohorts in the Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study (SLAS). We used SLAS1 as a development cohort to construct the risk assessment instrument, and SLA2 as a validation cohort to verify its generalizability.
The study was approved by the National University of Singapore Institutional Review Board.

Two distinct population cohorts were recruited in separate waves of recruitment of community-dwelling older adults in geographically different locations. SLAS-1 cohort participants who were aged 55 years and above and residents in the South East region of Singapore (N=2804) were recruited in 2003-2004 and were followed up at two re-assessment visits approximately 3 years apart in 2005-2007 and 2007-2009 respectively. The participants in the SLAS-2 cohort (N=3246) were aged 55 and above and residents in the South West region who were recruited in 2009-2013, with follow up assessments 3 to 5 (mean 4.5) years apart conducted in 2013-2018.
We evaluated the external validity of the SLAS-1 risk model by applying the prediction algorithm on individual participants in the SLAS-2 validation cohort.

In the NIC community –based interventional trial, the risk scores (ranging from 6 to 11) of 194 participants were evaluated on the trend of association with mean RBANS T-score of global cognitive performance using ANOVA with significance tests for linear trend.
Our risk index for predicting MCI was based on risk factors from a single study.
